result.topic_en: Special cases of an infinite product formula involving cubes (giving products of 1+(a/n)^3 in terms of Gamma functions and hyperbolic/trigonometric functions) and a related integral representation via Binet's formula for log Gamma.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 18 (57) (57) (2)

2. Suppose now that $\alpha = \beta$ in (4). We obtain
(6) $\left\{1+\left(\frac{2\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{2\alpha}{2+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{2\alpha}{3+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\cdots\cdots$
$= \frac{\{\Gamma(1+\alpha)\}^3}{\Gamma(1+3\alpha)}\cdot\frac{\sinh \pi\alpha\sqrt{3}}{\pi\alpha\sqrt{3}}$.
Similarly supposing that $\beta = \alpha+1$ in (4) we obtain
(7) $\left\{1+\left(\frac{1+2\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{1+2\alpha}{2+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{1+2\alpha}{3+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\cdots\cdots$
$= \frac{\{\Gamma(1+\alpha)\}^3}{\Gamma(2+3\alpha)}\cdot\frac{\cosh \pi(\frac{1}{2}+\alpha)\sqrt{3}}{\pi}$.
Since
$\left\{1+\left(\frac{\alpha}{n}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+3\left(\frac{\alpha}{2n+\alpha}\right)^2\right\} = \frac{1+\frac{\alpha}{n}}{\left(1+\frac{\alpha}{2n}\right)^2}\left(1+\frac{\alpha^2}{n^2}+\frac{\alpha^4}{n^4}\right)$
it is easy to see that
(8) $\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{1^3}\right)\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{2^3}\right)\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{3^3}\right)\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{4^3}\right)\cdots\cdots$
$\times\left\{1+3\left(\frac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}\right)^2\right\}\left\{1+3\left(\frac{\alpha}{4+\alpha}\right)^2\right\}\left\{1+3\left(\frac{\alpha}{6+\alpha}\right)^2\right\}\cdots\cdots$
$= \frac{\Gamma(\frac{\alpha}{2})}{\Gamma(\frac{1+\alpha}{2})}\cdot\frac{\cosh\pi\alpha\sqrt{3}-\cos\pi\alpha}{2^{\alpha+2}\pi\alpha\sqrt{\pi}}$.
3. It is known that, if the real part of $\alpha$ is positive, then
(9) $\log\Gamma(\alpha) = (\alpha-\frac{1}{2})\log\alpha - \alpha + \frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi) + 2\int_0^\infty \frac{\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{\alpha}}{e^{2\pi x}-1}\,dx$.
From this we can easily show that, if the real part of $\alpha$ is positive, then
(10) $\frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi\alpha) + \log\left\{\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{1^3}\right)\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{2^3}\right)\left(1+\frac{\alpha^3}{3^3}\right)\cdots\cdots\right\}$
$= \log\left(\frac{\cosh\pi\alpha\sqrt{3}-\cos\pi\alpha}{\pi\alpha}\right) - \frac{\pi\alpha}{\sqrt{3}} + 2\int_0^\infty \frac{\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\alpha}\right)^3}{e^{2\pi x}-1}\,dx$
Hence we see that
$\int_0^\infty \frac{\tan^{-1}x^3}{e^{2\pi\alpha x}-1}\,dx$
